# Results — Study 691 (Homing Pigeon) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect the
**homing-pigeon** geometry (a smaller **down** day whose real body sits fully inside a
larger prior **down** day's body — same-colour cousin of the
[harami](../../406-harami-pattern/)) by precise OHLC rules across the same fixed basket of
**26** liquid US large-caps + SPY used by the sibling candlestick studies (yfinance
**un-adjusted, price-only** daily bars), split by **prior 10-day trend** into the bullish
claim under test (shape after a **downtrend**, traded **long**), measure the **forward
1/3/5/10-day return** entered at the **next close** (one execution lag) against each
name's **unconditional base rate**, and run a HAC one-sample *t* + a label-shuffle placebo
+ a **Bonferroni** correction across the four-horizon family. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month).*

## Data stamp

- **Basket** (26, survivors, same panel as 403-hammer-hanging-man / 406-harami-pattern /
  684-inverted-hammer): SPY, AAPL, MSFT, JNJ, PG, KO, JPM, WMT, XOM, CVX, PFE, MRK, INTC,
  CSCO, HD, MCD, DIS, BA, CAT, MMM, HON, UNH, ORCL, PEP, COST, GS.
- **Span**: 1962-01-02 → 2026-06-30 · **345,846** daily bars · **5,154** homing-pigeon-
  shaped bars (any trend context).
- **Adjustment**: un-adjusted OHLC (the candle *shape* needs the printed levels); forward
  returns are therefore **price-only** (no dividends).
- **Content fingerprint** (panel, close columns over the basket): `8ddaab4e2e1e`. Companion
  single-name stamp (SPY OHLC, `quantlab.repro.data_stamp`): `7987ab25910e`
  (8,411 rows, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30).
- **Survivorship**: a fixed surviving-names basket — for this **bullish** claim the bias
  points *toward* finding a bounce (survivors recovered from dips that delisted names did
  not), so a null/weak result is **conservative**. Named on the Signal axis.
- **Multiple testing**: the same claim is tested across **four horizons** (1/3/5/10 days) —
  a Bonferroni correction (`p_adj = min(1, p_raw × 4)`) is reported next to the raw
  label-shuffle *p* for every horizon, not just the best one.

## The headline — HOMING PIGEON (shape after a downtrend), traded LONG, gross & net

The folk recipe: a shrinking down-day inside a bigger down-day shows sellers running out
of conviction — buy the bounce. Edge = conditional mean minus that name's base rate; net =
gross − 2 × 5 bps round trip (long-only, no borrow).

| Horizon | n | cond % | base % | **edge %** | win % | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* | Bonferroni *p* | net % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 2,885 | +0.170 | +0.066 | **+0.106** | 53.2 | **+2.58** | 0.001 | 0.005 | +0.006 |
| 3 days | 2,885 | +0.414 | +0.196 | **+0.224** | 55.7 | **+3.37** | 0.000 | 0.001 | +0.124 |
| 5 days | 2,882 | +0.576 | +0.324 | **+0.262** | 56.6 | **+3.16** | 0.000 | 0.002 | +0.162 |
| 10 days| 2,879 | +0.865 | +0.639 | **+0.244** | 58.0 | **+2.06** | 0.013 | 0.051 | +0.144 |

- Unlike its siblings (hammer, inverted hammer, harami), the pooled homing-pigeon edge
  clears **HAC *t* ≥ 2 at every horizon**, and the Bonferroni-corrected placebo survives at
  three of four (**10 days is the exception**, adjusted *p* = 0.051 — a hair over the 5%
  line). This is the most encouraging raw reading of the desk's five candlestick studies.
  The next three cuts are what keep the verdict at **Weak**, not **Real**.

## Alpha vs beta — does the SHAPE beat plain "buy any dip in a downtrend"?

The pigeon only ever fires *inside* a downtrend, where short-horizon mean reversion is
already well documented (De Bondt & Thaler 1985) — so the honest test isn't just "beats a
random day", it's "beats buying **any** day in the same downtrend, pattern or not." Welch
*t* of the pigeon's conditional return vs the pooled downtrend-only (no-shape-required)
return:

| Horizon | pigeon % | any-downtrend-dip % (n) | excess Welch *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | +0.170 | +0.094 (n=153,428) | +1.95 |
| 3 days | +0.414 | +0.259 (n=153,400) | **+2.37** |
| 5 days | +0.576 | +0.406 (n=153,377) | **+2.07** |
| 10 days| +0.865 | +0.707 (n=153,324) | +1.37 |

- The specific two-bar geometry adds something beyond generic downtrend dip-buying **only
  at 3 and 5 days** (excess *t* = 2.37 / 2.07). At 1 day (*t* = 1.95) and 10 days
  (*t* = 1.37) the pigeon's "edge" is statistically indistinguishable from just buying any
  dip in the same downtrend — **beta, not pattern-specific alpha**, at those horizons.

## The trend split matters — the 'wrong side' contrast

If the pattern is genuinely trend-conditional (not just any down-day pair, anywhere), the
*identical* shape traded long after an **uptrend** (the myth-check "wrong side") should
show a weaker or negative tilt:

| Horizon | n | edge (bps) | win % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 2,243 | −6.4 | 50.2 | −1.78 | 0.936 |
| 3 days | 2,242 | −3.1 | 53.2 | −0.51 | 0.651 |
| 5 days | 2,242 | −7.4 | 54.2 | −1.00 | 0.789 |
| 10 days| 2,238 | −9.9 | 54.2 | −0.85 | 0.794 |

Every horizon is flat-to-negative on the wrong side — unlike the inverted hammer's
"wrong-side" contrast (which stayed the *same sign*, undercutting its own trend story),
the homing pigeon's trend split genuinely discriminates: the downtrend context is doing
real work, not just window-dressing a pooled drift.

## The geometry alone — ANY (pooling both trend contexts), traded long

| Horizon | n | edge (bps) | win % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 5,152 | +3.0 | 51.8 | +1.12 | 0.133 |
| 3 days | 5,151 | +11.0 | 54.6 | **+2.37** | 0.007 |
| 5 days | 5,148 | +11.3 | 55.5 | +1.91 | 0.028 |
| 10 days| 5,141 | +9.4 | 56.3 | +1.03 | 0.128 |

Without the trend split, only the 3-day cut clears *t* ≥ 2 — confirming that the
downtrend condition is load-bearing for the claim, not incidental.

## Myth-check — does a shorter/longer lookback or a deeper washout rescue or weaken it? (H = 3)

| Variant | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain homing pigeon (trend lookback = 10) | +0.224 | +3.37 | 0.000 | 2,885 |
| trend lookback = 5 | +0.178 | +2.89 | 0.002 | 3,198 |
| trend lookback = 20 | +0.136 | +1.99 | 0.020 | 2,660 |
| min prior washout ≥ 5% | +0.274 | +1.68 | 0.013 | 822 |
| min prior washout ≥ 10% | +0.385 | +0.76 | 0.077 | 196 |

The result is fairly stable across a shorter or longer trend window (*t* = 2.89 to 1.99),
but demanding a *deeper* prior washout **does not** strengthen it — it thins the sample
and *weakens* the statistic (*t* falls to 0.76 on 196 events), the same
non-monotonic-filter signature the desk has flagged in the hammer and inverted-hammer
studies as evidence against, not for, a "deeper confirmation helps" refinement.

## Event clustering — is the pooled significance a handful of shared crash weeks?

Pooling 26 names' events only inflates a naive pooled *t* if the "many" events are really
a handful of shared market-wide dates (HAC corrects a name's own autocorrelation, not
cross-name co-occurrence). Across **2,887** pigeon-in-downtrend events (all bars with the
shape; two more than the 2,885 used in the forward-return tables above, which drop the two
events too close to the end of the sample to have a full forward window) spanning **1,345**
distinct ISO calendar weeks (1962→2026), the **busiest 10 weeks account for only ~3.9%**
of all events — no single crash episode (2008, 2020, 2022) dominates the sample. The
pooled significance is a broad, low-frequency tilt, not a repackaged macro event.

## Cost sweep (homing pigeon long, H = 3 — its best horizon)

| cost (one-way bps) | net edge (bps) |
|---|--:|
| 0.0  | +22.4 |
| 1.0  | +20.4 |
| 5.0  | **+12.4** |
| 10.0 | +2.4 |

Unlike the hammer / inverted-hammer / harami siblings — all net-negative at the desk's
standard 5 bps one-way — the homing pigeon's 3-day rule stays net-**positive** even at a
punitive 10 bps one-way. Costs are not what kills this pattern.

**3 of 26 names** (CVX, MCD, PEP) individually clear |*t*| > 2 — barely above the ~1.3
expected by chance at a 5% two-sided threshold across 26 independent draws, and 22 of 26
names show a **positive-signed** edge (a one-sided sign test the pattern does pass), but
almost none of them individually is *statistically* distinguishable from noise at
plausible per-name sample sizes (n ≈ 60–155). The pooled significance is a **broad,
consistent-direction, but individually-thin** tilt — not a robust idiosyncratic edge you
could hang a single-name trade on.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's a floor to find

On a deterministic OHLC panel (`data.synthetic_panel`) where we **plant** a genuine
post-homing-pigeon bounce, the same engine reads ≈ 0 with no edge and lights up hard when
one exists:

| planted bounce | events | edge % | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | win % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.000 (random walk) | 1,219 | −0.054 | −1.41 | 0.916 | 49.8 |
| 0.006 (real floor)  | 1,201 | +0.534 | **+13.61** | 0.000 | 65.4 |

Zero planted edge does not fake significance (*t* = −1.41, within noise); a genuine
0.6%/event floor is detected at *t* = 13.6. The real-tape reading is therefore a genuine
signal, not a blind harness — the pipeline can bank a planted effect when one is actually
there, which is what makes the real tape's more nuanced (partial) reading trustworthy
rather than a detector failing to look.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The pooled edge clears **HAC *t* ≥ 2 at all four horizons** (best
  +3.37 at 3 days) and the Bonferroni-corrected placebo survives at three of four (10-day
  adjusted *p* = 0.051, just over the line) — the strongest raw reading among this desk's
  five candlestick studies. But the decisive alpha-vs-beta cut (excess over buying *any*
  dip in the same downtrend) clears *t* ≥ 2 only at 3/5 days (2.37 / 2.07), not 1 or
  10 days — a real share of the pooled edge is generic downtrend mean-reversion, not
  shape-specific information — and only **3 of 26 names** individually clear |*t*| > 2,
  right at the chance baseline. Events are broadly spread (busiest 10 weeks = 3.9% of the
  sample) — not a repackaged crash artefact — but the edge is thin and non-robust
  per-name. The harness detects a *planted* floor at *t* = 13.6, so the reading is
  genuine, just fragile. (Survivorship tilts *toward* a bounce → conservative.)
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Net of a 5-bps round trip the 3-day rule nets **+12.4 bps**
  and stays positive even at 10 bps (+2.4 bps) — unlike every sibling candlestick study on
  this desk, costs are not what kills it. But a strategy that only 3 of 26 names carry
  individually, and whose edge is partly indistinguishable from a simpler "buy the dip in
  a downtrend" rule, is thin capital to deploy on the specific geometric claim rather than
  the cheaper substitute.
- **"Beats plain buying any downtrend dip?" — MIXED.** The shape's excess over the
  no-pattern-required downtrend base rate clears *t* ≥ 2 at 3 and 5 days but not at 1 or
  10 days — a genuinely split answer, not a clean confirm or bust.
